info.title: Finarthax API
info.description:
Personal finance API for Finarthax — accounts, transactions, recurring-transaction suggestions, budgets, goals, reports and settings.

## Authentication

Every route under **Protected** requires a NextAuth session cookie (`next-auth.session-token`, or `__Secure-next-auth.session-token` over HTTPS). The simplest way to test:

1. Sign in at `/login` in this same browser.
2. Come back to `/api-docs` and press **Try it out** — the cookie is sent automatically.

There is no bearer-token flow; the API is designed for the app's own browser session.

## Response envelope

Every JSON response is wrapped:

```json
{ "success": true, "message": "Success", "data": { } }
```

Validation failures return `422` with an `errors` object keyed by field name instead of `data`.

## Maintenance mode

When the `maintenance_mode` app setting is `true`, every non-`GET` request is refused with `503`. Reads keep working.

post.description: Creates the user, then bootstraps ten default categories and a default `Cash` account in the same database transaction. Rejected with `403` when the `allow_registration` app setting is off.
Stores a SHA-256 hash of a random token with a one-hour expiry and emails the plain token via Resend. Google-only accounts are rejected with `400`.

get.description: Returns every `app_settings` row flagged `isPublic` — landing-page copy, currency/language/theme options and feature labels. Values of type `json` are parsed before being returned.

get.summary: Look up a user's accounts and categories by email
get.description:
Used by the public quick-entry form so a transaction can be recorded without signing in.

**Balances are withheld by default.** This endpoint takes nothing but an email address, so returning balances unconditionally would let anyone who knows an address read that person's money. `balance` and `creditLimit` appear only when the account owner switches on the `publicQuickBalances` preference, and `showsBalances` always says which happened.

Rate limited to 20 requests per minute per client, since an unauthenticated lookup keyed by email is otherwise a convenient way to discover which addresses are registered.

post.summary: Record a transaction without a session
post.description: Same balance and budget bookkeeping as `POST /transactions`, but the owner is resolved from `email` instead of a session. Recurrence fields are not accepted here.

get.description: Reports database connectivity and process uptime. Returns `503` when the database is unreachable. Suitable for Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes. Note: this route is **not** wrapped in the standard response envelope.

post.description:
Delivers the weekly summary and the recurring-due reminder to every account that asked for them. Each send still passes the preference gate, so an account with `emailNotifications` — or the individual preference — switched off is skipped.

Authenticated with a bearer token rather than a session, because a scheduler calls it:

```bash
curl -X POST https://your-host/api/notifications/digest \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET"
```

Returns `503` when `CRON_SECRET` or the mailer is not configured.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Which digest to run. `recurring` suits a daily schedule, `weekly` a weekly one.

200.description: How many accounts were processed, sent and skipped

post.description: Refused with `400` once the `max_accounts_per_user` app setting is reached. Setting `isDefault` clears the flag on every other account. `creditLimit` is dropped unless the type is `CREDIT_CARD`.

get.description: Filtered and paginated, newest first. `search` matches the description case-insensitively.

post.description:
Creates the row and adjusts account balances and budget spend inside one database transaction. Set `isRecurring` with a `recurrenceInterval` to open a recurring series at the same time — the first suggestion is then scheduled one period after `date`.

Credit-card rules: `INCOME` on a credit card is refused with `422`, and a `TRANSFER` out of a credit card requires `toAccountId`.

recurringExpense.summary: Expense that opens a monthly series

put.description: The previous balance and budget effect is reversed before the new one is applied, so totals stay exact. Recurrence fields are not accepted here — use the recurring endpoints.

delete.description: Reverses the balance and budget effect before removing the row.

get.description:
Returns two kinds of suggestion.

**Scheduled** (`due`, `upcoming`) — series you track. `due` holds everything whose next occurrence is today or earlier; `upcoming` holds those within `lookaheadDays`.

**Detected** (`detected`, `dismissed`) — patterns inferred from history that are not tracked yet. A group needs at least `minOccurrences` occurrences, a median gap matching a known cadence, ≥60% gap consistency and a confidence of ≥55.

parameters.name: lookaheadDays
parameters.description: How far ahead a scheduled occurrence counts as upcoming

parameters.name: historyDays
parameters.description: How much history the detector reads

parameters.name: minOccurrences
parameters.description: Repeats required before a pattern is suggested

patch.summary: Start or stop tracking a series
patch.description: With `isRecurring: true`, every transaction matching the same pattern is stamped with a shared `recurrenceKey`, and the most recent one receives the schedule. With `isRecurring: false`, the schedule is cleared across the whole series — past transactions are untouched.

post.description:
Creates a real transaction from the anchor — balances and budgets move exactly as they would for a manual entry — and hands the schedule to the new row, advanced by **one** period. Confirming repeatedly therefore backfills a series that was missed for months.

An empty body is valid: the amount, date, description, accounts and category all fall back to the anchor. When confirming a *detected* pattern (which has no series yet), send `interval` so the series can be created.

Moves the schedule to the next date in the future without creating anything — one call catches up a series that is several periods overdue. Returns `422` when the transaction is not part of a series. If the new date passes `recurrenceEndDate`, the schedule is cleared and the series ends.

Stamps `recurrenceDismissedAt` on every transaction in the group, so a later occurrence does not resurrect a suggestion you already rejected. The pattern still appears under `dismissed` in the overview.
Refused with `400` once the `max_categories_per_user` app setting is reached.
Upserts on (user, category, month, year). On creation, `spent` is backfilled from the expenses already recorded in that month, so a budget added mid-month is immediately accurate.

patch.description: Sets `currentAmount`. The goal flips to `COMPLETED` automatically once it reaches its target.

get.description: This month's income, expense, transfer and net balance with per-type counts, the same figures for last month, the percentage change between them, every account with its balance, and the five most recent transactions.
Six months of income/expense/transfer totals, spending grouped by category, budget progress and transfer flow.
Totals, savings rate, average daily expense, largest transaction, top categories, a day-by-day spending trend and the full transaction list.
Twelve-month breakdown plus averages, savings rate, top categories, and the best and worst month by net balance.

post.description: Adds a per-account breakdown (including transfer in/out) and a daily trend on top of the monthly report's figures. The end date is extended to `23:59:59`.

get.description: Includes `passwordChangedAt` and `passwordExpiresAt` so the UI can warn before a password expires.

post.description: Verifies the current password, then resets `passwordChangedAt` and `passwordExpiresAt` from the `max_password_age_days` app setting.

get.description: Returns a generated PDF rather than the JSON envelope.

delete.description: Removes the user and, by cascade, every account, transaction, category, budget, goal and setting that belongs to them. Irreversible.

get.description:
Returns the account's preferences, reconciled against the catalogue first: keys added to it are created with their default, keys removed from it are deleted. A value the user chose is never overwritten, so this is safe to call on every page load.

Each row carries a `type` (`boolean`, `string`, `number`) that says how to render it, and a `category` that groups it on the settings screen. For a preference offering a fixed set of choices, the options live in the public app setting named `<snake_cased key>_options` — `dateFormat` → `date_format_options`.

200.description: Preferences, ordered by category then key

patch.description: Values are stored as strings regardless of the setting's declared type — send `"true"`, `"80"` or `"dd/MM/yyyy"`. Returns `404` for a key that is not in the catalogue.

get.description: Returns `token`, `expire`, `signature` and `publicKey` for a direct browser upload to ImageKit. Expiry is capped at one hour.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The ImageKit file id stored as `avatarFileId`

cronSecret.description: The `CRON_SECRET` value, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. Used only by the digest endpoint, which a scheduler calls without a browser session.

sessionCookie.name: next-auth.session-token
sessionCookie.description: NextAuth JWT session cookie. Sign in at `/login` in the same browser and it is sent automatically — there is no token to paste. Over HTTPS the cookie is named `__Secure-next-auth.session-token`.

TransactionId.name: id
TransactionId.description: Id of the transaction that anchors the series. For a detected pattern, use `detected[].transactionId` from `GET /recurring`; for a tracked series, use `due[].transactionId` or `upcoming[].transactionId`.

TransactionResponse.description: The transaction, with its account, destination account and category expanded

Maintenance.description: Maintenance mode is on — writes are refused

example.message: App is under maintenance. Please try again later.

skipped.description: Accounts blocked by a preference, or with nothing to report

balance.description: Negative on a credit card — the magnitude is the debt owed

toAccountId.description: Transfers only. Null means the money left your accounts entirely (e.g. an ATM withdrawal).

recurrenceKey.description: Shared by every occurrence of one series

nextOccurrence.description: Set on the newest occurrence only — this row is the series anchor

recurrenceDismissedAt.description: Set when the user asked not to be shown this pattern again

spent.description: Maintained incrementally as transactions are written

PublicAccount.description: An account as the public quick-entry page sees it.

balance.description: Present only when the owner enabled `publicQuickBalances`. Negative on a credit card — the magnitude is the debt.

creditLimit.description: Present only when the owner enabled `publicQuickBalances`.

showsBalances.description: False when the owner keeps balances private, so the UI can explain rather than show zeros

value.description: Always a string, whatever the declared type

type.description: Which control the settings screen renders

category.description: Groups the preference into a card

value.description: String, or a parsed object/array when `type` is `json`

ScheduledRecurrence.description: A tracked series, described by the transaction that currently anchors its schedule.

transactionId.description: Pass this as `{id}` to the recurring actions

DetectedPattern.description: A repeating pattern inferred from history that is not tracked as a series yet.

transactionId.description: The most recent occurrence — pass this as `{id}` to the recurring actions

monthlyCommitted.description: Monthly cost of tracked recurring expenses

monthlyPotential.description: Monthly cost of detected but untracked recurring expenses

password.description: At least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter and one digit

creditLimit.description: Ignored unless the type is CREDIT_CARD

toAccountId.description: Transfers only, and must differ from `accountId`

isRecurring.description: Open a recurring series from this transaction

TransactionUpdateInput.description: Every field except `type` is optional; `type` selects which shape is validated.

keepTracking.description: Set false to log this occurrence and end the series
